data: This course introduces algorithmic concepts and hands-on experience in the use of relevant tools/techniques for many key biological sequence analysis problems in Bioinformatics/Computational Biology. We will introduce various algorithms and heuristics for pairwise sequence alignment, multiple sequence alignment, molecular evolution and phylogenetic analysis, genome sequencing and annotation. The students will be introduced to the key algorithms and their applications of key Bioinformatics tools like BLAST and its variants, CLUSTALX, tools like PHYLIP for phylogenetic and evolutionary analysis. This course will be cross listed with Computer Science and assumes a prior background in either “Introductory Biology” or “Discrete Mathematics” and will be open to third and final year students majoring in Biology/Computer Science/Mathematics.
